findings.title: Bind COMMIT_READY resolution to the exact action type
findings.description: The new _progress_sources guard verifies the S36 manifest, policy, action_parameters_hash and query_basis_hash but never checks S36.action_type. An otherwise coherent S36/S37 pair for another action type therefore advances the attempt to COMMIT_READY. Action parameters may be identical across action types whose policy obligations differ; validating parameter bytes alone is not exact action binding. Frozen DB S36 explicitly requires the action and manifest/policy identity, and the packet requires coherent source-bound S36/S37 prerequisites.
findings.reproduction: Independently invoked the actual RepositoryTransaction._progress_sources at the reviewed SHA using a fake cursor supplying the exact immutable snapshot/F/D/N/resolution/validation rows and matching prior source bindings. With S36.action_type=WRONG_ACTION_TYPE, matching current execution basis, hashes, policy, manifest, request, epoch, expiry and semantic/envelope PASS, the method returned all sources without GuardRequired. This is a direct source-guard reproduction, not PostgreSQL DC evidence.
findings.impact: AdvanceAttempt can persist COMMIT_READY using a resolution computed for a different action policy. This finding concerns the internal progression prerequisite; no T6 authorization bypass or production execution expansion is claimed.
findings.requested_change: Derive the required action type from the exact authenticated TEST policy/action basis and reject mismatching S36.action_type before advancing. Bind that identity in the query/certificate basis as appropriate under the existing frozen model. Add an immutable input-only wrong-action-type mutant with otherwise self-consistent hashes, and verify actual guarded AdvanceAttempt denies with exact no effects. Rerun required task checks and obtain fresh SHA-bound reviews.
